text:
maria: Quick sync — proposing we collapse the current per-artifact quant blobs into a small inheritance stack (base -> model -> deployment override). The goal is fewer edge cases at runtime and simpler rollbacks.

aj: Curious about the rollback story. How does inheritance help when we need a fast revert to a safer config?

maria: If a deploy override causes regressions we can flip the deployment-level flag to inherit base immediately. No model rebuild. Also plan to timestamp and hash each effective profile for quick verification.

sasha: Please add a signed_version field in the profile. Ops can attest stable profiles, runtime verifies signature before applying hot changes. Helps with cross-team ownership.

dave: Signed profiles sounds good but worrying about latency on verify path. Maybe runtime caches verified signatures for N minutes.

lin: Another angle — we should expose a light-weight runtime response that tells caller which profile was used and why (e.g., "used:base-v3, reason:capacity-fallback"). That helps debugging.

eva-ml: +1. Also need a scalar "quality_delta" reported per request so we can aggregate regressions without pulling full evals. Not a perfect metric but helpful for ops.

maria: Draft API sketch for runtime handshake:
```
request: { model: "m-mnlf", prompt, hints: { budget_ms: 120, prefer_lowbit: true } }
response: { text, profile_applied: "base:v3#sig", degrade_reason: "fp8->int8_hysteresis", quality_delta: -0.02 }
```

sasha: Nice. Two notes: 1) make degrade_reason an enum with freeform detail field for traces; 2) quality_delta should be optional and normalized across models.

aj: How do we compute quality_delta cheaply? Running evals per request not feasible.

eva-ml: We use lightweight heuristics: token-level confidence drift + a small LM-based consistency check on a tiny anchor prompt set. Cheap but noisy. Aggregate over windows.

dave: On implementation: runtime should never accept profile overrides that widen quant mismatch beyond a threshold compared to baseline. i.e., enforce a max_allowed_loss field in the profile metadata.

lin: That brings up versioning — profile compatibility rules: additive relaxations allowed, tightening requires canary and signed approval.

maria: Exactly. Proposal: three gates — local sim smoke, shadow traffic sampling, canary traffic. Only after these pass can ops sign the profile for rollout.

sasha: How will ops observe regressions? Need telemetry hooks: per-profile histograms of latency, token-error proxies, and the quality_delta heatmap.

eva-ml: Also capture a small sample of model outputs (anonymized) for quick human review when alerts fire. Keep privacy controls.

ops-bot: Deploy check: canary=red for profile base:v4 on m-mnlf; reason=quality_delta>0.03 over 10m. Tagging @maria @sasha

maria: Thanks bot. I'll roll back the override and start a shadow run for the alternative fp8 calibration.

aj: One last operational thing — add a profile "eviction_ttl" so runtime can auto-revert cached applied overrides after N seconds if telemetry absent. Prevents stale misconfigs.

maria: Good call. I'll update the RFC doc with these fields: signed_version, max_allowed_loss, eviction_ttl, quality_delta semantics, and the handshake contract. Will post link once updated.

sasha: If you can also include a short migration plan for existing profiles (how to map fields) that'd be helpful for oncall.

maria: Will do. Thanks all.
